comments.text: The single pass fixes the reported case, but it drops the legacy email-priority behaviour the issue refers to. Lookup now strictly follows the IdentityFields order, so with identityFields ["username", "email"] and an email-formatted identity that equals one record's email and another record's username, the username match wins. Previously (and in earlier versions) email was always tried first; this silently changes which account a credential resolves to for existing configurations. Keep email first when it is configured and the identity is email-formatted, e.g. by stably sorting `email` to the front of a cloned identity field list before the loop.
The removed code was the only visible use of `list.ExistInSlice` in this hunk; verify the `list` import is still used elsewhere in the file or remove it, otherwise the package won't compile.
No regression test was added for an email-formatted username with `email` absent from identityFields, nor for the email-vs-username priority.
